items.title: Millions of Australians could have no say in who inherits their super
items.description: New research shows most Australians have not made a legally binding death benefit nomination to ensure their superannuation goes to who they want it to when they die. And many funds do not make it easy.

items.title: Police working to determine how long body in suitcase lay by road
items.description: Police are still working to identify human remains found in a suitcase by the side of a road in southern NSW.

items.title: How a simple request for AI to book a gym class exposed a major threat
items.description: When Andrew asked his AI personal assistant to book him a spot in a gym class, he had no idea he would accidentally initiate an autonomous cyber attack.

items.title: The end of the low interest rate era is here and it weighs on house prices
items.description: We seem to have flipped from worrying about rising house prices to worrying about falling house prices. Well, some of us have, anyway.

items.title: Israeli government rejects Trump's Gaza peace plan
items.description: Israeli Prime Minster Benjamin Netanyahu says Hamas's proposed plan for disarming is "unacceptable", rejecting the Trump administration's plans to end fighting in the Palestinian territory.

items.title: Australia has the most expensive cigarettes in the world, and now a booming black market
items.description: After decades as a world leader in tobacco control, Australia now finds itself in troubled waters. But those trying to find solutions are far from on the same page.

items.title: Albanese is the opposite of Rudd and that comes with its own risks
items.description: Cabinet's indecision on support for Tony Burke's immigration cuts shows a key difference between Anthony Albanese and Kevin Rudd.

items.title: NRL clubs split on playing Alameddine brothers over gang war concerns
items.description: Escalating gangland tensions see a junior member of the Alameddines benched from playing rugby league, but his brother has been given the green light to play.

items.title: Who killed Tupac? Three decades later, there may finally be answers
items.description: Three decades after the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur, the world may get some answers about who killed the young superstar, and why.

items.title: Aviation bosses summoned, airport workers stood down after Sydney near-miss
items.description: Airservices Australia's CEO has been summoned to meet with the federal Transport Minister after a near-miss at Sydney Airport on Sunday.

items.title: Regional emergency departments a 'basket case of mania', doctor warns
items.description: The most dysfunctional emergency departments in Victoria are in regional areas, according to data, with doctors describing overcrowded corridors, lapses in patient safety and burnt-out staff.

items.title: 'Not going to be around for much longer': Small business under pressure despite population growth
items.description: Mount Barker is one of South Australia's fastest-growing districts, but while some businesses are excited about the prospect of more customers, others are competing with tightening wallets and operating pressures.

items.title: Live: ASX set to lift after Wall St hit another record close
items.description: The ASX is expected to hit a fresh record high after Wall Street's S&P 500 also closed at a record. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Live: Bulk-billing rates on the rise
items.description: The federal government says the number of Australians seeing a GP for free is on the rise. Follow live.

items.title: How Elliot won Race Around the World in 'opportunity of a lifetime'
items.description: After 100 days making films in different countries, Race Around the World winner Elliot Constable credits one particular approach for his success.

items.title: What are the rules for taking carer's leave from work?
items.description: When it comes to taking time off work for your own personal illness or injury, you probably have some idea of what your entitlements are. But when it comes to needing time off to care for others, you may be more unsure of your rights.

items.title: History quiz: Show us what you know about 90s pop culture and musical masterpieces
items.description: We'll also test you on the Paris Olympics, the 2017 parliamentary citizenship scandal and history-making Test cricket.

items.title: Conflict of interest questions raised as Qld deputy premier approves planning changes
items.description: Queensland Deputy Premier Jarrod Bleijie personally approved town planning changes championing house development in a zone where landowners included a developer who had just donated $50,000 for a private lunch with the politician.

items.title: Big changes for NSW renters as portable bond scheme begins
items.description: The NSW government's portable rental bond system starts today and will cost renters who want to use the online service $25.

items.title: Flights cancelled, evacuations as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
items.description: Typhoon Dolphin makes landfall in densely populated eastern China, meteorological authorities say, after the storm triggered more than 1,000 flight cancellations, evacuations and a top-level alert.

items.title: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says 50,000 North Korean troops will help Russia in war
items.description: The Ukrainian president took to social media to announced "a decision has been made for 30,000 to 50,000 North Koreans to be deployed on the territory of Russia", while calling on South Korea to provide support for Ukraine's air defence.

items.title: Alleged Irish international crime boss charged
items.description: Daniel Joseph Kinahan was flown from Dubai to Dublin, the UAE state news agency reported, after his arrest in April, to face allegations about "serious organised crime offences".

items.title: Paramilitary promises video of Iran's supreme leader unseen since March
items.description: Video of Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since he assumed the role in March, has been promised by a paramilitary leader.

items.title: Wind in the wilderness a real threat to unprepared hikers
items.description: Bushwalker and meteorologist Urshla Connor knows from personal and professional experience that being prepared for changing weather can make all the difference between a beautiful hike and a life-threatening situation in Tasmania's wilderness.

items.title: Wildfire forces more than 20,000 people evacuate homes in western Canada
items.description: Thousands of people in British Columbia have been ordered to flee a fast-moving wildfire that nearly doubled in size overnight.
